findings.who: A filer whose 2023 Form 4952 showed a carryover on line 7. They took the standard deduction in 2024 and filed no 2024 Form 4952, so the disallowed interest still carries forward into 2025, where they itemize.
findings.why_no: The child question asks only about 'line 7 of a 2024 Form 4952 of either of you'. No 2024 Form 4952 exists, so the truthful answer is no, even though a carryover from 2024 into 2025 exists.
findings.irs_text: f4952 p. 3, Who Must File: 'You don't have any carryover of disallowed investment interest expense from 2024'; p. 1, Part I, line 2: 'Disallowed investment interest expense from 2024 Form 4952, line 7'
findings.fix: Ask whether either spouse has investment interest expense disallowed in any earlier year that has not yet been deducted. Say this includes a carryover from a year in which no Form 4952 was filed, for example because the standard deduction was taken. Then ask for the amount: line 7 of the last Form 4952 filed, less any part deducted since.

findings.who: A filer who was required to file Form 4952 for 2024 but left it off the return in error. On a joint return, the case can also be one spouse whose 2024 carryover was figured but never put on a filed form.
findings.why_no: The child question ties the yes to a filed 2024 Form 4952's line 7. Without a filed form, the filer truthfully answers no, though the IRS text treats the carryover as a fact ('carryover ... from 2024'), not as a document.
findings.irs_text: f4952 p. 3: 'Use Form 4952 to figure ... the amount you can carry forward to future years'; 'You don't have any carryover of disallowed investment interest expense from 2024'
findings.fix: Ask about the carryover as a fact. Ask for line 7 of the 2024 Form 4952 when one was filed; otherwise ask the filer to figure the 2024 amount (line 3 minus line 6 for 2024).

findings.who: A filer whose prior-year software produced Form 4952 automatically, for example from margin interest or Schedule K-1 investment interest. The software carried an amount to line 7, but the filer never noticed it.
findings.why_no: The parent question asks, in its own words, whether 'either of you have investment interest expense carried forward from an earlier year'. A filer who never saw the carryover answers no from memory, without checking the prior return. The parent question does not point to line 7 or to the 2024 return.
findings.irs_text: f4952 p. 1, Part I, line 2: 'Disallowed investment interest expense from 2024 Form 4952, line 7'
findings.fix: In the parent question's help, tell the filer to check whether either spouse's 2024 return (joint or separate) included Form 4952 and whether its line 7 is more than zero. Add that margin interest and K-1 investment interest can produce one.

findings.who: A filer whose only link to investment interest is a carryover, or K-1 investment interest from a partnership or S corporation, where they personally borrowed nothing.
findings.why_no: The parent question begins 'pay or accrue any interest in 2025 on money borrowed for investments' and ends 'Answer Yes if any of these applies:', but the list is not shown. A filer may read the list as the whole rule and skip the carryover clause. Without the list, it cannot be confirmed that it names carryovers.
findings.irs_text: f4952 p. 3: 'Include investment interest expense reported to you on Schedule K-1 from a partnership or an S corporation'; 'You don't have any carryover of disallowed investment interest expense from 2024'
findings.fix: Make sure the list after 'Answer Yes if any of these applies' names, as its own item, a carryover shown on line 7 of any spouse's 2024 Form 4952 or left over from an earlier year.

locators: p. 1, Part I, line 2, "Disallowed investment interest expense from 2024 Form 4952, line 7"
p. 1, Part I, line 2, "Disallowed investment interest expense from 2024 Form 4952, line 7"; p. 3, Who Must File, "You don’t have any carryover of disallowed investment interest expense from 2024"

findings.who: A limited partner or S corporation shareholder whose 2025 Schedule K-1 reports investment interest expense. The entity, not the filer, borrowed on margin or took a loan to carry its portfolio, and the filer has no loan of their own.
findings.why_no: The gate asks whether 'you (or your spouse) pay interest on money borrowed to buy investments.' The filer borrowed nothing and paid nothing directly, so no is the truthful answer. Neither the gate nor its help mentions Schedule K-1.
findings.line: f4952.line1_if_interest (and, through it, f4952.carryover_if_interest and f4952.line4g_if_interest)
findings.irs_text: f4952 p. 3, Line 1: "Include investment interest expense reported to you on Schedule K-1 from a partnership or an S corporation."
findings.fix: Add a separate prong to the gate: 'or does a Schedule K-1 from a partnership or S corporation (yours or your spouse's) report investment interest expense?' The help should say the entity's borrowing counts even if you borrowed nothing yourself.

findings.who: A filer or spouse with interest accrued in 2025 but not yet paid. Examples are an accrual-method item passed through to them, or interest on an investment loan that accrued under the loan terms and was capitalized into principal or deferred to 2026.
findings.why_no: The gate asks only whether they 'pay interest.' Nothing was paid in 2025, so they answer no.
findings.irs_text: f4952 p. 3, Line 1: "Enter the investment interest expense paid or accrued during the tax year, regardless of when you incurred the indebtedness."
findings.fix: Ask whether they 'pay or owe (accrue) interest,' as the helper wording already does ('pay or accrue').

findings.who: A filer who holds, without limited liability, a working interest in an oil or gas property in which they do not materially participate, and who borrowed to acquire or fund it.
findings.why_no: They regard a working interest as a business or drilling venture, not 'investments such as a margin loan from a broker,' so they answer no.
findings.irs_text: f4952 p. 3, Property held for investment: "A working interest in an oil or gas property that you held directly or through an entity that didn't limit your liability is property held for investment, but only if you didn't materially participate in the activity."
findings.fix: Add to the help: 'Investments include stocks, bonds, funds, land held for appreciation, royalty interests, and a working interest in oil or gas that you don't materially work in.'

findings.who: A filer who borrowed to buy royalty-producing property, an annuity-type income stream, or land held only for appreciation, or who borrowed to buy into a partnership or S corporation that holds portfolio assets.
findings.why_no: The only example, 'a margin loan from a broker,' reads as the whole category. The filer does not see a loan for land, royalties or an entity interest as 'money borrowed to buy investments.'
findings.irs_text: f4952 p. 3, Property held for investment: "includes property that produces income, not derived in the ordinary course of a trade or business, from interest, dividends, annuities, or royalties. It also includes property that produces gain or loss ... from the disposition of property that produces these types of income or is held for investment."
findings.fix: Broaden the examples in the gate help to land held for appreciation, royalty interests, and buying into a partnership or S corporation that holds investments. Say that the list is not complete.

findings.who: A filer who says yes to the gate because they took a home equity loan or HELOC and used the proceeds to buy stock.
findings.why_no: The gated question tells them to 'Leave out interest on a home loan.' They omit interest that is investment interest, because the proceeds were traced to investments and were not used to buy or improve the home.
findings.irs_text: f4952 p. 3, Line 1: "Investment interest expense is interest paid or accrued on a loan or part of a loan that is allocable to property held for investment"; Allocation of Interest Expense: "If you paid or accrued interest on a loan and used the loan proceeds for more than one purpose, you may have to allocate the interest."
findings.fix: Reword to 'Leave out interest on a loan used to buy, build or improve your home. Interest on a home equity loan whose money went into investments counts.'
